video.title: When You Get A Low Forehand

classification.reason: The coach explicitly instructs players to tilt their torso and have their chest almost face the ground when preparing for a low forehand.

problem.title_as_question: What should you do when you get a low forehand?
problem.definition: How to position the upper body on a low forehand to maintain a normal striking mechanic.

quotes.text: When you get a low forehand, tilt your torso.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: That'll let you strike the ball the way you normally do.
quotes.speaker: coach

quotes.text: If the ball is sufficiently low, your chest can almost be facing the ground as you prepare.
quotes.speaker: coach

symptoms.description: Difficulty striking a low ball the way you normally do.

causes.statement: Failing to tilt the torso prevents you from striking the low ball using your normal mechanics.

angles.summary: Tilting the torso allows the player to strike a low ball with normal swing mechanics.
On sufficiently low balls, the chest can be oriented almost facing the ground during preparation.

solutions.summary: Tilt your torso when you get a low forehand, letting your chest almost face the ground during preparation if the ball is sufficiently low.
